faq.tdee.a: TDEE, total daily energy expenditure, estimates all the calories you burn in a day: your BMR at rest plus everyday movement and exercise. It is often called maintenance calories, the intake that keeps your weight about the same.
faq.difference.q: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
faq.difference.a: BMR is the energy your body uses at complete rest. TDEE multiplies BMR by an activity factor, from 1.2 for little or no exercise to 1.9 for a physical job or training twice a day, so it is always higher than BMR.
faq.use.q: What can I do with my TDEE?
faq.use.a: Use it as a reference point for a daily calorie goal: eating about your TDEE keeps intake and burn roughly balanced, eating less is a deficit and eating more is a surplus. It is a starting estimate, so compare it with how your weight actually changes over a few weeks.
